summary: A steel fire tower on Crescent Lake NWR, standing and registered in August 2026; its build date is unresolved between a 1937 WPA report and early-1940s CCC statements.

facts.design: lookout tower (material not confirmed for this site; the 1937 item's 100-foot steel tower is not named)

events.note: WPA work began at the Garden county refuge, per the Jan 31, 1937 Nebraska State Journal item quoted on the register; the item says crews built a 100-foot steel lookout tower, without naming the tower
Registered August 9, 2026 as US 1845, NE 3; nominated by Admin

evidence.supports: item dated January 31, 1937: WPA work at the Garden county refuge began in 1936, with relief laborers improving the site
evidence.quote: January 31, 1937: "At the Garden county refuge, work was started by the WPA in 1936, and 25,208 'man hours' was devoted by relief laborers in improving it.

evidence.supports: the 1937 newspaper (Nebraska State Journal) says crews built a 100-foot steel lookout tower; the item does not name the site
evidence.quote: They built a 100 foot steel lookout tower ... (Nebraska State Journal)

evidence.supports: the same item lists a service building and seed storage cellar
evidence.quote: service building and seed storage cellar

evidence.supports: USFWS says the refuge has two such towers, built early 1940s by the CCC
evidence.quote: The fire tower is one of two such structures built on the Refuge in the early 1940's by the Civilian Conservation Corps.

evidence.supports: towers no longer used for fire observation; they serve wildlife
evidence.quote: Although the towers are no longer used for fire observation, they are serving wildlife.
Administered by U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service
Crescent Lake South Garden 41.72859 -102.41997 Tower Standing

evidence.supports: refuge offers recreation to thousands of visitors each year
evidence.quote: Crescent Lake National Wildlife Refuge provides numerous recreational opportunities to thousands of visitors each year.

evidence.supports: trails and roads may be impassable after a recent wildfire and extreme dry conditions
evidence.quote: Due to a recent wildfire and extreme dry conditions, refuge trails and roads may be impassable, even with 4-wheel drive vehicles.

evidence.supports: refuge protected in 1931 for wetlands, migratory birds and other animals
evidence.quote: Crescent Lake NWR was protected in 1931 to ensure the wetlands would continue to be protected, providing migratory bird species and other animals a safe haven.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Not resolved. The register quotes a 1937 newspaper saying WPA work began in 1936 and crews built a 100-foot tower, without naming the site. It also quotes USFWS placing both refuge towers in the early 1940s by the CCC. The north page dates its own 60-foot tower to 1935. The story reports all three.

sources.title: Crescent Lake National Wildlife Refuge - Visit Us

notes_for_editor: Build date unresolved (see resolved_conflicts). The 100-foot figure comes from the 1937 newspaper item and does not name which refuge tower it describes, so no height_m was set; the north page gives 60 ft for its own tower. Primary source to try: the FWS press release 'U.S. Improves Duck Refuge in Nebraska (Crescent Lake Refuge)', June 12, 1937 (fws.gov archive; PDF is 19370612.PDF on the media page, not reached: a guessed URL returned 404). Access not established; the FWS visit page does not mention the towers. Read budget used: 6 page reads and 2 WebSearch calls. Register nominator is 'Admin'.
